_meta.source: registry.npmjs.org (direct GET per candidate name) + pypi.org/pypi/<name>/json (direct GET per candidate name)

context: Fountain (fountain.com) has no fountain-hire/@fountain-scoped npm package per Discovery's cheap probe. This sweep does a direct GET against registry.npmjs.org/<name> and pypi.org/pypi/<name>/json for every plausible official-SDK name, to close the absence claim to the gold-standard direct-lookup method (per project practice, see Brandlight packages dimension).

npm_hits_investigated.name: fountain
npm_hits_investigated.evidence: author Giulian Drimba <giuliandrimba@gmail.com>, repo github.com/giuliandrimba/fountain, first published 2012-12-08 (2 years before Fountain the hiring company was founded in 2014), latest version 0.3.4, no homepage set. Personal open-source project, no connection to fountain.com.

pypi_hits_investigated.name: fountain
pypi_hits_investigated.evidence: summary 'Parses fountain screenplay markup', author gabriel montangé láscaris-comneno <gabriel@tibas.london>, homepage bitbucket.org/gabriel.montagne/fountain, version 0.1.3. Screenplay-markup parser (same family as npm's fountain-js), no connection to fountain.com.

pypi_hits_investigated.name: fountain-sdk
pypi_hits_investigated.verdict: unrelated namesake, REJECTED (see raw/fountain-sdk-namesake.json for full disambiguation)
pypi_hits_investigated.evidence: summary 'Python SDK for Fountain stablecoin API' — a crypto/stablecoin product on the XRP Ledger, repo github.com/xrpl-fountain/fountain-sdk-python (org+repo now 404/deleted on GitHub as of capture date), author listed as 'Fountain Team <support@fountain.com>' which superficially matches the hiring company's real support address but the product description (stablecoin API, JWT email-auth, admin dashboard endpoints, XRPL org name) is entirely unrelated to Fountain's frontline-hiring/workforce domain. Treated as a coincidental/likely-fake author-email namesake, not the real Fountain SDK.

docs_sdk_mention_check.result: no mention of an official SDK, client library, npm package, or pip package anywhere in the docs index or the two API-overview pages. Docs describe a REST-only API (OAuth2 client_credentials + legacy X-ACCESS-TOKEN header), authenticated via curl examples only — no 'Libraries'/'SDKs' page or section exists in the ~185-page reference index.
